prompt: Use Pattern and Matcher to find the first YYYY-MM-DD substring inside a larger text, returning null when there is none. Complete firstDate in DateExtractor.
explanation: Unlike matches(), Matcher.find() scans forward through the text looking for the pattern anywhere inside it, and returns true at the first hit. \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} spells out the digit counts with the {n} quantifier, and group() with no argument returns exactly the substring the last successful find() matched. Calling group() is only legal after find() returned true, which is why the null case is handled first.
hints: Pattern.compile(...) builds the regex once; pattern.matcher(text) gives you a Matcher for this specific text.
\d matches one digit and {4} repeats it exactly four times. Remember the doubled backslashes inside a Java string.
if (m.find()) return m.group(); -- otherwise return null. find() locates the pattern anywhere in the text.
